author_explicit: HUNL uses separate flop and turn counterfactual-value networks plus an auxiliary preflop network.
Postflop network: seven fully-connected hidden layers, 500 nodes each, PReLU.
Inputs: pot size as a fraction of total stack plus two player ranges encoded into 1000 buckets each.
Outputs: counterfactual values for both players, interpreted as fractions of pot.
Outer differentiable correction enforces zero-sum by subtracting half the summed weighted game-value error.
Flop re-solving uses 1000 CFR iterations, 500 omitted, and the turn network at next-street boundaries.
Postflop buckets: 1000 clusters generated by k-means with earth mover distance over hand-strength-like features.
Training: Adam, average Huber loss, batch 1000, lr 0.001 then 0.0001 after 200 epochs, approximately 350 epochs.
policy: Fail closed when an original/reconstruction bucket artifact has not been explicitly supplied; never silently invent a mapping.
reconstruction_choices: HUNL PReLU instantiated with one learned slope per hidden layer, anchored to released DeepStack-Leduc nn.PReLU() default convention; HUNL paper itself does not state scalar-vs-per-unit parameterization.
Frozen 1326 hand ordering remains project-canonical; no claim that it reproduces private HUNL serialization.
Flop-to-turn pair-conditioned chance aggregation is 1/45, from exact Holdem blocker algebra.
released_code_anchored: Input ordering [P1 range | P2 range | pot feature].
Zero-sum algebra is raw - 0.5*dot(raw, concatenated ranges), broadcast to every output coordinate.
At a chance boundary, ranges are bucketed, normalized conditionally per next board, NN values are multiplied by opponent-compatible range mass, then inverse-bucketed.
Next-round values remember post-skip opponent mass and weighted CFVs for later get_value_on_board conditioning.
Released tree node pot is min(node.bets), i.e. per-player matched committed amount, and is divided by stack before NN input.
